QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_73

question.text: Nari Shakti Trust runs TWO programmes: (i) SHG-based women empowerment (SAS-400), and (ii) women-owned financial-inclusion bank accounts with micro-insurance (SAS-1300). 120 SHG women have opened first-time bank accounts. Under the cross-standard SIA engagement, the SIA should:

answer.text: Pick whichever standard the SE prefers

Assess each programme/outcome under the relevant SAS thematic area (gender indicators under SAS-400, financial-inclusion indicators under SAS-1300) and clearly scope and report each in line with the applicable standard
Combine all outcomes under SAS-100 only

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook expects each programme/outcome to be assessed under the relevant SAS thematic area, with the assessment scope and reporting aligned to that standard. SHG-based women empowerment work falls under SAS-400 (gender-related indicators), while financial-inclusion bank accounts and micro-insurance fall under SAS-1300, and each should be reported accordingly. The Trap: Option A surrenders SIA independence and standard selection. Option C collapses thematic substance into the umbrella standard. Option D shirks scope by dropping one thematic area. Note: The choice of standard follows the activity and reporting scope, not the SE's preference.
